column1: a relatively sharply defined and cohesive invasive front, smooth or pushing tumor margins, and an absence or extreme rarity of detached small cellular islands in the adjacent peritumoral stroma.
an irregular or jagged invasive margin, characterized by a moderate dispersion of small, disconnected cellular aggregates breaking away from the main tumor mass into the adjacent reactive stroma.

a highly infiltrative, hazy, and ill-defined invasive front, widespread dissociation of the tumor mass, and numerous fine cellular aggregates extensively dispersed deep into the prominent desmoplastic stroma.

continuous malignant epithelial structures, with 0 to 4 detached single tumor cells or small clusters (comprising fewer than 5 cells) visible within the desmoplastic stroma at the advancing edge of the tumor.
partial loss of epithelial cohesion, with 5 to 9 detached single tumor cells or small clusters (comprising fewer than 5 cells) scattered within the dense peritumoral stroma at the invasive front.

severe loss of cellular cohesion, featuring 10 or more detached single tumor cells or small clusters (comprising fewer than 5 cells) densely infiltrating the peritumoral stroma, frequently accompanied by an active fibrotic reaction.
